cards.explanation: The answer is Jerusalem. The man says he's heading out to measure it, to find its width and length (Zechariah 2:2). He didn't say he was just wandering around with that measuring line. Somebody had a plan, friends.

The answer is a city without walls. The message says Jerusalem will be a city without walls because of the multitude of men and livestock within it. So the man with the measuring line is heading out to measure a city that is going to have a lot of people and animals in it, friends.

The answer is False. The message never mentions enemies knocking walls down. It says Jerusalem will be a city without walls because of the multitude of men and livestock within it. Then it adds that the LORD says, "For I will be a wall of fire around it…" (Zechariah 2:5).

The answer is a wall of fire. The LORD says, “For I will be a wall of fire around it, declares the LORD…” So the city has no walls, but it isn't left without protection. The LORD says He Himself will be the wall, friends.
The answer is True. In the same breath as the wall of fire, the LORD says, “…and I will be the glory within it.” So He is around the city and inside it too. That's both ends covered, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “Get up! Get up! Flee from the land of the north…” and He says He scattered them like the four winds of heaven. That is a call to leave, not to stay. Two "Get up!"s in a row is the kind of wake-up call I could have used back when I was stuck in the back of a junk drawer.

The answer is the apple of His eye. The LORD of Hosts says, “…for whoever touches you touches the apple of His eye…” The apple of the eye is something you guard with everything you have. So the text says anyone who touches His people has touched something He guards closely, friends.

The answer is that their own servants plunder them. The one speaking says, “I will surely wave My hand over them, so that they will become plunder for their own servants.” So the nations that plundered God's people become plunder themselves. And it's their own servants who take it.

The answer is True. Verse 9 ends with the one speaking saying, “Then you will know that the LORD of Hosts has sent Me.” The nations that plundered will become plunder for their own servants. And then God's people will know who sent him, friends.

The answer is that He is coming to dwell among them. The LORD says, “Shout for joy and be glad, O Daughter of Zion, for I am coming to dwell among you…” The joy comes from Him coming to live among them. Not from anything else in the neighborhood, friends.

The answer is people. The LORD says many nations will join themselves to Him on that day, “…and they will become My people.” Then He adds, “I will dwell among you…” Many nations, and they're His people, friends.

The answer is True. The passage ends with, “Be silent before the LORD, all people, for He has roused Himself from His holy dwelling.” All people are told to be silent. The reason comes right with it: He has roused Himself from His holy dwelling.
